name: Nicholas Burt
lead: I'm a software engineer with experience spanning Apple's engineering and customer systems groups. My work focuses on Swift/XCUI test automation, data integrity across distributed service pipelines, and behavioral validation for AI-assisted systems, backed by a BS in Computer Science and full-stack cloud development

paragraphs: I fell in love with programming when I learned how to automate away repetitive tasks at work. Back then, I didn’t know much about software development, but I could immediately see the power in handing labor over to code. My earliest automations were crude: direct mouse and keyboard manipulations and quick JavaScript snippets. They broke constantly. A dropped network connection, a slight shift in the OS or UI, or an unexpected data type would bring everything down. That friction taught me an essential lesson early on: writing good software is challenging not because of syntax, but because it has to contend with the real world in all its messy glory.

Studying Computer Science transformed my practical curiosity into formal engineering. I learned how to represent the physical world through abstract models and define truth inside closed systems. I explored the creative capabilities of game programming, studied coordinated communication protocols across networks, and learned to manage conceptual complexity through object-oriented design.

I graduated knowing I had built a strong foundation, but also convinced that there was still so much more to master. Moving into enterprise software development, I see how much that balance really counts. At enterprise scale, it is no longer just about writing code that works in isolation. It is about building resilient, maintainable systems that can absorb unexpected failures, adapt to evolving scale, and deliver dependability where it matters most.
